text.en:
MALACAÑANG
PRESIDENTIAL DECREE No. 688 April 22, 1975
RETURNING TO THE CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION THE POWER TO GIVE APPROPRIATE
EXAMINATIONS FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS.
WHEREAS, the Civil Service Commission as the Central Personnel Agency had been giving the teacher
examinations until the approval and promulgation of Republic Act No. 6040 on August 4, 1969, in which it
was provided in Section 9 of said Act that the Department of Education shall give " . . . . the appropriate
examinations for public school teachers with the assistance of the Civil Service Commission."
WHEREAS, the Civil Service Commission has better facilities than the Department of Education and Culture
to give the appropriate examinations for public school teachers; and
WHEREAS, to give meaning and substance to Article XIII (A) and (B) of the New Constitution, it is
necessary to return to the Civil Service Commission the power to give appropriate examinations for public
school teachers.
NOW, THEREFORE, I, FERDINAND E. MARCOS, President of the Republic of the Philippines, by virtue
of the powers vested in me by the Constitution, do hereby declare and decree that:
The Civil Service Commission shall give appropriate examinations for public school teachers to establish
register of teacher eligibles from which certification may be made whenever teacher eligibles may be needed
for appointment.
This decree is hereby made part of the law of the land and shall take effect immediately.
Section 9, paragraph 7 of Republic Act 6040 amending Section 23 of Republic Act 2260, insofar as the
teacher examinations are concerned and all provisions of other Acts and Decree inconsistent with the
provisions of this Decree are hereby repealed.
Done in the City of Manila, this 22nd day of April, in the year of Our Lord, nineteen hundred and
seventy-five.
